```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
ld <- read.csv(here::here('analysis/data/carryover-sensitivity/ladder/ladder-long.csv'))
fam <- ld |> filter(level == 'family')
pick <- function(f, a, q) {
  x <- fam |> filter(family == f, analysis == a, quantity == q)
  stopifnot(nrow(x) == 1)
  x
}
f3 <- function(x) sprintf('%.3f', x)
rv <- readRDS(here::here('analysis/data/carryover-sensitivity/referee-variants/block-T/summary.rds'))
trend_g9 <- rv$reject[rv$method == 'E7cr2' & rv$c_bm == 0]
pooled <- read.csv(here::here('analysis/data/carryover-sensitivity/referee-reanalysis/m2-pooled-size.csv'))
sz9 <- pooled$reject[pooled$item == 'pooled' & pooled$method == 'G9']
sz8 <- pooled$reject[pooled$item == 'pooled' & pooled$method == 'G8']
dif <- pooled[pooled$item == 'paired G9 vs G8', ]
cov <- read.csv(here::here('analysis/data/carryover-sensitivity/referee-reanalysis/m3-coverage.csv'))
cov9 <- cov[cov$level == 'summary (mvn cells)' & cov$method == 'G9', ]
g9_sizes <- sapply(1:7, function(f) { x <- fam |> filter(family == f, analysis == 'G9', quantity == 'size'); if (nrow(x)) x$value else NA })
```

**Purpose.** G9 is the analysis we recommend for the biomarker-by-drug interaction in a Hybrid aggregated N-of-1 trial when carryover is present and the carryover half-life is unknown. It was the best of the analyses evaluated in a staged simulation under the correlation encoding of the interaction.

**Model.** For participant $i$ at visit $t$, with $w_{it}$ the week of the visit,
$$Y_{it}=\beta_0+\beta_B B_i+\beta_w w_{it}+\beta_D D_{bc,it}(h)+\beta_{BD}\,B_i\,D_{bc,it}(h)+u_i+\varepsilon_{it},$$
$$u_i\sim N(0,\sigma_u^2),\qquad \operatorname{Corr}(\varepsilon_{it},\varepsilon_{is})=\varphi^{|w_{it}-w_{is}|},\qquad
D_{bc,it}(h)=\begin{cases}1&\text{on drug}\\ 2^{-t_{sd,it}/h}&\text{off drug after exposure}\\ 0&\text{before first exposure.}\end{cases}$$
The half-life is chosen from the data, $\hat h=\arg\min_{h\in\mathcal T}\mathrm{AIC}\{M(h)\}$ with $\mathcal T=\{0.25,0.5,1,2\}$ weeks and AIC from maximum-likelihood fits. The selected model is refitted by restricted maximum likelihood. The interaction is tested with $T=\hat\beta_{BD}/\mathrm{SE}_{CR2}(\hat\beta_{BD})$ against a $t$ distribution with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, where
$$\mathrm{SE}^2_{CR2}=\Bigl[(X^\top WX)^{-1}\sum_i X_i^\top W A_i\,\hat e_i\hat e_i^\top A_i^\top W X_i\,(X^\top WX)^{-1}\Bigr]_{BD,BD},\qquad A_i=(I-H_{ii})^{-1/2}.$$

**Notation.** $B_i$: baseline biomarker, centered. $D_{bc,it}$: exposure-decayed drug indicator. $t_{sd,it}$: weeks since the last discontinuation (0 before exposure). $h$: analysis half-life; $\hat h$: its selected value. $u_i$: participant random intercept. $\varepsilon_{it}$: residual with continuous-time AR(1) correlation $\varphi$. $\beta_{BD}$: the interaction, the change in drug effect per unit of biomarker (under the correlation encoding $-c_{bm}\sigma_{BR}$ per standard deviation of the biomarker at the true half-life). $X_i$, $W$, $\hat e_i$, $H_{ii}$: participant design matrix, working weights, residuals, and leverage block. CR2: the bias-reduced cluster-robust variance estimator (Bell and McCaffrey).

**Why G9.** The ladder adds one change at a time (original analysis E0; G1 binary drug with AR(1); G6 adds CR2; G8 adds exposure decay at the true half-life; G9 selects the half-life). Pooled over the corrected original grid (Hybrid, OL+BDC and CO; $N$ of 35 and 70):

```{r tab}
rows <- c('E0', 'G1', 'G6', 'G8', 'G9', 'F1')
what <- c('Original analysis', 'Binary drug, AR(1)', '+ CR2 inference', '+ exposure decay, true $h$', '+ selected $\\hat h$ (recommended)', 'Expectancy terms, fixed $h$')
tab <- data.frame(Analysis = rows, Change = what,
  Size = sapply(rows, function(a) { x <- pick(1, a, 'size'); sprintf('%.3f (%.3f)', x$value, x$mcse) }),
  Power = sapply(rows, function(a) { x <- pick(1, a, 'power'); sprintf('%.3f (%.3f)', x$value, x$mcse) }))
knitr::kable(tab, format = 'latex', row.names = FALSE, booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, linesep = '',
  col.names = c('Analysis', 'What changes', 'Null rejection (MCSE)', 'Power at $c_{bm}=0.45$, $t_{1/2}=1$ (MCSE)')) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 8, position = 'center')
```

**Scenarios tested** (G9 in every one; each with a null and a power cell unless noted). Designs: Hybrid, OL+BDC and crossover, $N$ of 35 and 70, half-lives 0, 0.5 and 1 week. Misspecified decay: Weibull shapes 0.5 and 2 analyzed as exponential; true half-lives 0.2, 2 and 4 weeks. Serial correlation 0.5 and 0.9. Dropout: completely at random and dependent on baseline severity, 10, 20 and 30 percent. Prognostic biomarkers: correlation with the placebo response, the natural course and baseline severity, 0.3 and a feasible ladder to 0.8. Large $N$ of 140 and 280 (null only). A biomarker that predicts the natural-history trend and a patient-specific slope. A Hybrid run with eight null and eight power cells at 5,000 and 1,000 replicates.

- **Size.** G9 rejects at `r f3(pick(1,'G9','size')$value)` under the null, against `r f3(pick(1,'E0','size')$value)` for E0, which is liberal, and `r f3(pick(1,'G1','size')$value)` for G1, which is conservative. Across seven scenario families (misspecified decay, serial correlation, dropout, prognostic pathways, large $N$, trend) its pooled size is `r f3(min(g9_sizes, na.rm = TRUE))` to `r f3(max(g9_sizes, na.rm = TRUE))`.
- **Power.** G9 has `r f3(pick(1,'G9','power')$value)` power, the same as G8 (`r f3(pick(1,'G8','power')$value)`), which needs the true half-life. It exceeds G1 (`r f3(pick(1,'G1','power')$value)`) and F1 (`r f3(pick(1,'F1','power')$value)`). E0 has higher raw power only because it rejects too often.
- **No pharmacokinetic input.** The analyst supplies a grid, not a half-life. Power matches the true-half-life analysis even though the selected value is spread over the grid.
- **Costs, stated.** Selection adds `r sprintf('%.4f', dif$reject)` (paired SE `r sprintf('%.4f', dif$mcse)`) to size over G8 (`r f3(sz9)` against `r f3(sz8)` pooled over the null cells), and its 95% interval covers about `r sprintf('%.2f', min(cov9$mean_cov_lower))` to `r sprintf('%.2f', max(cov9$mean_cov_lower))` of the time. A fixed 1-week half-life with CR2 avoids selection, holds nominal size, and stays within two points of G8's power.
- **Limits.** The results hold under the correlation encoding, in the Hybrid design, on one parameter set. A biomarker that predicts the natural-history trend inflates the size of every analysis examined; G9 rejects at `r f3(trend_g9)` at $N=70$.
